title: love burns
content:
I think love makes us a little crazy and the best ones turns us totally mad

But nevertheless, we’re not supposed to stop, 
not to give up, 
not to stop trying because if one doesn’t work, 
then the next one might 

But the uncertainty is great and the repercussions, painful 

And in all the woes love can cause, 
the department that serves the greatest injustice is unrequited 

That, that hurts more than anything you could ever feel

Especially when they start like they might love you back, 
stay with you, care.

But then, because you felt or thought they were real, 
you’ll let your guard down and you’ll love them back, 
you’ll go all in 

But because they never really wanted you, 
they’ll feel choked 
They wouldn’t understand why you care so much, 
they just wanted to have fun

So, they’ll leave, because they never meant to stay

And that’s why unrequited love hurts most sometimes 

Because someone is giving their all and the other person just isn’t.

title: reels
content:
I woke up this morning with a subtle smile,
Despite the troubled thoughts of yesterday,
Despite the anger I fell asleep with.
Despite the restless night i had.
Morning came, and with it a gift —
The thought of you.

title: reels
content:
You’re one of those rare souls life blesses us with,
The kind of presence that feels like sunlight
Breaking through the heaviest storm clouds.
You’re like the quiet rainbow after the rain —
Proof that no matter how dark the night,
There’s always a dawn worth waiting for.
And for me, that dawn
So often comes in the thought of you.

title: reels
content:
You’re beautiful —
Not only in the way the world sees beauty,
But in the depth of your spirit,
In the kindness of your heart,
And in the way you effortlessly bring peace into chaos.
Whenever life feels heavy,
Whenever the world feels unfair,
You shine through like hope wrapped in human form.

title: reels
content:
You’re my safe space,
The one who reminds me that life
Can still be soft, gentle, good
Even when it feels otherwise.
You make me believe that true friendship
Isn’t about how often we meet or speak,
But about how deeply we carry one another
In our hearts.
And trust me,
I carry you with me,
always.

title: beauty
content:
this is a reminder that you're beautiful.

Your laughter has magic.
It doesn’t just echo;
It lingers, it heals.
Your smile?
It’s a window to the beauty of your soul.
And your heart…
Oh, your heart is something
poets could write books about.
You might not realize
How much light you bring into other people’s lives —
How you give without trying,
How you inspire without even knowing it.
how to some people,
You’re like that rare melody
That once heard, never leaves the mind.
and to others,
that gentle fragrance
That lingers long after it passes by.


You give hope.
Hope that goodness still exists in its purest form.
In a world that feels too fast,
Too cold, too distant.
You’re a reminder
That sometimes God doesn’t send angels with wings,
He sends people like you —
People who feel like home
Even when the world feels like anything but.

title: love
content:
I need you to always remember this:
You are precious.
You are valuable.
You are loved.
On days when you feel small,
When you doubt yourself,
When the world tries to make you feel
Like you’re not enough,
Know that you are more than enough.
You are extraordinary.
Anyone who gets to know you,
Even for a moment,
Should count themselves blessed

Whoever doesn’t love or make you feel it?
It’s their loss, they have no idea about you,
And I’d sincerely like to interfere and scream
“Wake up! You have love right here!”
But I can’t, cos It’s not my place anymore.
I wish i could do something like magic
To make your wish and heart desires come true,
Even though I can’t,
I’d love to try, cos, whoever has that privilege,
Of being loved by you, even if it’s minute,
Should count themselves blessed!
So blessed they got something extraordinary,
like you.

title: reels
content:
I hope today gives you back
Even a fraction of the joy you bring to others.
The world is so much better with you in it —
And my world, especially,
Wouldn’t shine the same without you.

title: a love poem
content:
i want to remind you that you're beautiful,
not the kind of beauty that fades when the light goes out,
but the kind that glows from within and stays,
even on your hardest days.

You’ve been that gentle reminder that even in this noisy world,
there are still quiet miracles.
and you're one.

sincerely believe me,
You’re beautiful — in every sense of the word.
Not just in the way your eyes glimmer when you talk about something you love,
or the way your laughter spills out softly like windchimes in a morning breeze,
but in the calm that lives behind it all, behind everything!.

Your beauty isn’t loud — it’s felt.
It lingers, like a melody that stays in your head long after the song ends.

And don’t get me started on the little things
your nose, your lips, your hands, your fingers 
each detail of you is crafted like a verse in a poem I could read forever.
Even the way you tilt your head when you’re curious,
or how your face softens when you’re lost in thought.
I notice it all (you can say I'm obsessed, yeah, sorry, not sorry).
You’re like a living poem — every gesture, a line worth remembering.

Your eyes? they speak — softly, deeply — like they’ve seen both storms and sunrises.
Your voice? that calm melody I could listen to forever,
the kind that settles chaos and makes the world sound right again.
And your smile… it could rebuild anyone’s hope in seconds.
You are, without exaggeration, art — every line, every word, every breath.

But beyond that beauty, there’s strength, yeah.
You’ve carried things many people would’ve broken under,
and you still find ways to smile,
to give,
to love.

You’re the kind of person who turns pain into poetry
and exhaustion into grace.

title: reels

and the distance grows

that you find happiness so real,
so full,
so freeing,
that it makes Heaven smile.

this attachment,
it’s not control, it’s not possession. 
It’s that quiet, sacred kind of love where you just want the person to know they’re safe, valued, and adored, loved, cherished and..... more.

title: Assurances
content:
You know what’s strange?
I don’t yearn for you in the way the world defines yearning.
It’s not about having you —
It’s about being around you,
Knowing you’re okay,
Hearing your laughter somewhere in this same world.
You make me want to be gentle.
You make me want to guard your peace, not take from it.

If I could, I’d wrap you in calm instead of my arms,
I’d hold your heart, not your body.
Because what I feel isn’t hunger —
It’s reverence.
You’re something I want to cherish, not consume.

So even if I never get to call you mine,
I’ll still thank God for you
Because people like you don’t just cross paths;
They shift lives.
And you’ve shifted mine in ways words will never explain.

You’ve shown me that beauty isn’t just in what we see —
It’s in what we feel when someone walks into our life
And suddenly makes breathing feel easier, 
Yeah, i might’ve stolen your line there.
You’re that for me.
A breath of calm in a noisy and dusty environ.

And if you fall, I’ll fall with you,
Just to make sure you land softly.
If you rise, I’ll rise too,
To make sure the wind never hurts your wings.

It doesn’t matter what the world calls us —
Friends, strangers, a weird kinda friendship, whatever.
I know what I feel when I think of you:
A quiet promise,
To always choose kindness when it comes to you.

So when life gets loud,
When the world feels unkind,
And you start to forget who you are,
I’ll be here to remind you.
That you’re strong.
That you’re beautiful.
That your heart was made of light,
Even when everything around you feels dark.

I’ll be here to whisper that you are loved, you are enough.
You are everything good that you doubt about yourself, yeah.

And maybe one day, when life slows down,
You’ll look back and see this, see me,
And realize someone out there truly saw you, 
Even if you didn’t believe you were up to it,
Saw the light behind your words,
The fire behind your gentleness and the ocean behind your silence.

title: friendship
content:
I’ve always had much luck with companions

They go and come and there’s never not a multitude of them

But maybe I should have said that I’ve never had much luck 

Because the plentiful of a thing does not assure it’s competence ever!


This fact,  I’ve had to learn and relearn 

Because I’m hard of hearing and coarse of heart 

And I believed softness didn’t pay except when you had to be a fool

For your companions, to keep your circle, stay in the clique, to be relevant, famous, loved....

To hurt beautifully,
And smile with pain coated lips and well......

What dreadful tale is this?

The most terrible parts of friendships I’ve always been dealt with,
And I had thought you had to burn painfully for anything you get

Because it’s norms, this is normal

And after a while, I burned out
 But I kept piling the fuel so I can be plump and red in face
While becoming an empty husk inside

I knew journeys were never ever straight,
They criss-cross and have sharp turns and dangerous bends

And friendships are always full of differences
Like opposite opinions and clashing contradictions 

And that was all it was
And it was so for a long while.

But suddenly there was you
And in your wake, change 

Like little hands raised to prayer
Like the innocence of a new dawn breaking
The newness of an incoming seasoning
The toothless smile of a new born 

You’re to me like new things brought forth from awesomeness 
And the purity of their newness is unparalleled 
And..,......

I’ll always be grateful to your silent lending hands 
Your beauty coated not in flesh but in humanity, dare I say divinity


And again, 
New turns appeared in my path 
And they were brighter than before

And I’ve been learning,
To burn beautifully, without pain
You’ve given me a friendship that has blended into other things that words cannot suffice to describe

And I cherish this, 
Will cherish and protect this
Till I can guide you onwards, towards the right path
Like you’ve done for me
Now and always.

 And I hope, desperately clings-

title: What We Carry
content:
We carry mornings we couldn't name
and nights that left their fingerprints on our ribs.
We carry the quiet chores of becoming—
how a small kindness can tilt a whole day,
how grief returns like a tide that knows the shore.

There are rooms we leave the light on for,
conversations we only finish in our heads,
and the simple miracle of breath meeting breath—
someone asking, "How are you?" and waiting for the real answer.

We are not unfinished. We are unfolding.
We are not late. We are learning the clock of our own hearts.
And if today all you carried was yourself
from one moment into the next—
that's still a kind of sun rising.

title: Between Your Name and Mine
content:
We learned to talk in weather—the warm fronts,
your laughter; the storm warning, my silence.
Some evenings we were windows reflecting windows;
some mornings we were a door that opened.

There is a country between your name and mine
where ordinary things become holy:
the cup you set down, the minute that lingers,
the hand that doesn't forget how to return.

If love is a grammar, we are still syntaxing,
still choosing the gentle conjunctions—
and yet, and also, despite, still.
Come sit with me in the soft grammar of us,
where we keep discovering new ways to say home.

title: The Ledger
content:
I kept a ledger of almosts:
calls unsaid, doors unknocked, roads unwalked.
It was a heavy book, and I kept it close,
as if shame were a kind of passport.

But one day I counted backwards—
how every almost taught me a tenderness,
how every no saved a soft portion of me
for a truer yes I hadn't met yet.

I do not forgive the past. I befriend it.
We share a bench. We watch the river.
When it asks if I would change anything,
I say: only the distance I kept from my own heart.

title: Study Break
content:
Some nights the book is heavier than its pages,
and the clock forgets mercy.
You measure your worth in highlighters and margins,
in the slim applause of checkmarks.

Listen: your brain is not a machine—it is a meadow.
It needs sky, and a minute with wind in it,
and a friend who reminds you your name isn't a grade.

Let the problem rest in its own ink.
Let your shoulders remember what ease feels like.
There is a kind of learning that happens
only when you look up and briefly love the world again.

title: When It Piles Up
content:
It doesn't rain for days—it stacks.
Plates in the sink of the soul, emails like hail.
So many small futures asking to be answered.

Start with a square inch of possible:
one breath, a glass of water, a corner cleared.
Call a friend and borrow their horizon.
Let the list forgive you for being human.

Remember: mountains are moved by knees and minutes,
by the humble choreography of now.
You do not have to fix your life.
You only have to love one piece of it long enough to stay.

title: Practice of Light
content:
This is not denial. This is discipline—
to name the small lamps as they appear:
steam rising from a cup, a bird insisting on morning,
your own pulse counting you worthy.

Hope is not a mood; it's a practice.
Like watering plants that haven't bloomed yet,
like saving a seat for someone you haven't met.
Today, let your faith be ordinary and stubborn—
the way the sun keeps showing up for windows.

title: People I Have Been
content:
I have been the loud room and the quiet chair,
the last to leave and the first to worry.
I have been both apology and echo,
and I have learned to bless each version.

If you meet me on a day I am small,
know I am saving space for someone else inside me.
If you meet me on a day I am bright,
know you are seeing the light that others handed me.

We are a relay of kindness, a hand-to-hand dawn.
And even when we forget each other,
we keep the sky lit for the next traveler.

title: After the Storm
content:
You don't have to hurry your mending.
Even the shore negotiates with the sea.
Pick up the pieces that know your name,
leave the ones that belonged to the wave.

One day, you will laugh and not flinch at the echo.
One day, tenderness will knock and you will let it in.
Until then, be a harbor to yourself—
deep enough for rest, shallow enough for light.

title: Apartment Thermostat
content:
The heat clicks on like a promise,
and the plant leans toward a window I forgot to clean.
I burn the toast and butter it anyway;
we call these small mercies breakfast.

Outside, a bus sighs into its morning—
people making a living out of showing up.
I practice it here: feet on floor, cup in hand,
learning again how to belong to an ordinary day.

title: Call Your Friend
content:
Call the one who knows your middle name
and the way you went quiet after August.
Don't rehearse the script. Let the pauses carry their own weight.
Say: I'm okay and also I'm not.

Hear their laugh fold the room into a safer shape.
Remember: you are not a burden. You are a bridge—
made strong by every foot that trusted you across.
